decisions.decision: Change the documentation, not the implementation: remove the ready-to-proposed (revise) and leased-to-paused edges from the Increment lifecycle in docs/architecture/domain-model.md section 5.
decisions.rationale: docs/product/user-facing-spec.md section 5 makes paused a Requirement state, and section 6 forbids synchronising Increment status with Requirement status, so IncrementStatus.Paused is not required by the user-facing specification. Pausing work on an Increment is expressed by a Control Intent whose scope already admits an Increment, together with the Requirement paused state. Re-proposal is expressed by creating a new Increment rather than returning an existing one to Proposed, which is what the same section already requires when it forbids overwriting an Artifact.

decisions.decision: Keep the closure test's declared edge table as the single machine-checked transcription of the diagram, and update only its comment about the documentation gap.
decisions.rationale: The test asserts equality between the accepted edge set and a declared table, so once the diagram matches the implementation the comment describing a gap becomes false. The assertion itself needs no change, which is the evidence that the drift was in the prose.

decisions.decision: Correct the test-count prose in the ev-v2-010-domain evidence artifact from 27 to the measured 26 while leaving every measured number and both evidence keys untouched.
decisions.rationale: The M1 gate judgement independently measured 26 top-level tests (16 baseline plus 10 new). An evidence record that overstates its own scope is a record defect even when the substantive claims hold; correcting the count keeps the artifact trustworthy without erasing any observation.

risks: Removing edges from a diagram can hide a genuine requirement; the mitigation is that the closure test fixes the accepted edge set, so a future implementation change that adds an edge fails the test rather than silently diverging again.
Editing an evidence artifact requires recomputing its hash in the index; the ledger test enforces that, so a partial edit fails loudly.
